lead.headline: Tate's back is a fresh tweak; Pickens opens the week with 28
lead.deck: Your second receiver hurt his back in Thursday's drills and has one practice left. Your flex scored 28.0 last night and you lead 28–1 with eight starters to play.
lead.body: Start with the bad news about your own players. Carnell Tate's back listing has a cause now, and it is not reassuring: ESPN's Turron Davenport watched him tweak it during individual drills at Thursday's practice and go to the head trainer. He finished the session limited. No Titans coach has spoken, ESPN has left his projection at 13.6, and he has one practice before a game status. Saquon Barkley did not practise on Wednesday or Thursday and Philadelphia's beat writers expect him to miss London; he is on your bench at 0.0 either way. Alvin Kamara was limited on Thursday. Now the good news. George Pickens, claimed on Wednesday at the cost of your waiver priority, caught nine of thirteen targets for 130 yards and a touchdown in Dallas's 24–16 loss to Tampa Bay: 28.0 in your flex. CeeDee Lamb had two catches before his quadriceps tightened and he left with six minutes to play. Your opponent, Kings of the North, started the Cowboys' defence and got one point. You lead 28–1, ESPN projects 133.6 to 110.1 and gives you 63%; they still have Tee Higgins in their flex at zero and will find about eleven points when they fix it. Among leaguemates, Kings of the North dropped Kenny Gainwell and Michael Pittman Jr. on Thursday for the Cowboys' defence and Devaughn Vele. Your lineup is the projection lineup and nothing needs doing this morning. Read Tennessee's report this afternoon, and at 09:30 on Sunday read the inactive list: if Tate is on it, Matthew Golden takes his slot. Make no claim; you are last in the order.
